label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 1, pool timeouts 174

report.summary: After the 04:30:02 restart the DB pool was cut to 1 connection with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session then blocked the only connection, causing pool timeouts, 503s and slow transfers.

findings.claim: At 04:30:02 the app restarted with poolMaximumSize 10→1 and connection timeout 30000→250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed pool settings at the restart inside the window.

findings.claim: With a single connection, borrowers queued and timed out: 174 acquisition timeouts, pending up to 2, only during 04:30:03–04:30:58.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show timeouts and saturation within the post-restart interval, with a max of 1.

findings.claim: A session idle in transaction blocked a ledger_app session (up to ~2 s) from 04:30:04 to 04:30:58, holding the one connection and stalling requests.
findings.reason: Blocker samples show a 24-sample block matching the pool-saturation interval.

findings.claim: Transfers failed (500×24, 503×107, ratio 0.32) with p95 1.2 s and p99 2.2 s, consistent with pool exhaustion rather than the downstream consumer.
findings.reason: The error and latency symptoms coincide with the pool-starved period; the tiny pool made the blocker's impact severe.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery to the consumer is healthy (282/282 success, ~71 ms); the stuck failed=619 and old undelivered age are pre-existing and unchanged.
findings.reason: Deliveries all succeeded, and arrivals match publications, so the consumer is not the cause.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2 s, and the identity and origin of the idle-in-transaction session (44179) are unknown.
Counters restarted, so request counts span both sides of the restart and are not split into before and after.
next_checks: Identify what session 44179 is and why it was idle in transaction, e.g. from application or DB logs.
Review why the pool was reduced to 1 with a 250 ms timeout (dirty revision) and restore the previous settings.

alternatives.reason: All deliveries succeeded at ~71 ms with no server or network errors.
alternatives.hypothesis: Slow or failing downstream consumer causing transfer slowness

alternatives.reason: Arrivals equal publications; the failed count of 619 is constant and predates the window.
